AFL Season 2026 - Simulation App



R

Machine Learning

Statistical Modelling

Shiny

Monte Carlo



XGBoost model of the 2026 regular home and away season with GenElo, Team Attack/Defence Rating, Player Rating (Individual player 10gma) and Travel distance as inputs. Static input Monte Carlo simulation for the season with prediction uncertainty increasing with time to the game. Team ability inputs and uncertainty is user adjustable. Fixture difficulty by Elo and travel difference included.





Jan 31, 2026












Brownlow Medal Model



R

Machine Learning

Statistical Modelling



This post walks through the full workflow for building an ordinal regression model with random effects to predict the Brownlow Medal. Using AFL data from fitzRoy R package, player-game are used to estimate player-specific biases through a mixed model. These random intercepts are then incorporated into an ordinal model to generate vote probabilities for every match. Monte Carlo simulations are used to recreate the umpire voting process and estimate each player’s chances of winning.

Gender Reveal Betting App



R

Shiny

Market Making



Fun app to bet on a gender reveal or any two horse race. The odds update with each bet to show the current betting sentiment and naively balances the odds. Very open to market manipulation with no overround or if the odds are actually known to be 50/50.

Habit Tracking Retro Web App



CSS

Typescript

React

SQL



A fitness and habit tracking PWA built with React, TypeScript, and Supabase. Inspired by the “cassette futurism” aesthetic of Alien and Blade Runner, it features an authentic CRT terminal interface with amber phosphor glow effects and scanlines. CSS and aesthtic taken from this repo https://github.com/Imetomi/retro-futuristic-ui-design. The offline-first architecture uses localStorage for instant responsiveness, syncing seamlessly to the cloud when online. Can be installed as a native app on any device—no app store required.

text:
The source for any page in your website could also be a Jupyter Notebook. This one is third-post/index.ipynb.
Here’s an example I borrowed from the Seaborn docs:

import seaborn as sns

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Load the diamonds dataset
diamonds = sns.load_dataset("diamonds")

# Plot the distribution of clarity ratings, conditional on carat
sns.displot(
    data=diamonds,
    x="carat", hue="cut",
    kind="kde", height=4, aspect=1.5,
    multiple="fill", clip=(0, None),
    palette="ch:rot=-.25,hue=1,light=.75",   
)
